gaps.explanation: All funds agree with the p5 Statement of Revenues, Expenditures, and Changes in Fund Balances - Governmental Funds except Special Assessments. p12 Budgetary Comparison Schedule - Special Assessments Fund (budgetary basis) prints Total resources actual 334,991 (Property 309,379, Intergovernmental 16,835, Special assessments 8,774, Interest 3); the p5 Special Assessments column prints Total revenues 333,594 (Property 309,026, Intergovernmental 16,835, Special assessments 7,730, Interest 3). Difference 334,991 - 333,594 = 1,397 (Property 353 + Special assessments 1,044) = the gap of -1,397. Other funds: General 3,368,293 (pp15-16 = p5), Street 2,840,744 (p11 = p5), EMS 779,007 (p13 = p5), Other Governmental Funds 26,489 (p14: 184 + 437 + 15,868 + 10,000 = p5). Both printed totals are correct for their basis; no detail fix.

Budgetary-basis schedules (p11-p13) differ from the GAAP p5 statement columns: Street p11 Total charges to appropriations 2,732,158 vs p5 Street Total expenditures 2,814,733 (short 82,575: public works 595,792 vs 580,343; capital outlay 1,963,176 vs 2,060,487; debt service 173,190 vs bond fees 16,888 + principal 124,990 + interest 32,025 = 173,903); Special Assessments p12 401,720 vs p5 401,198 (over 522: debt service 398,932 vs 391,600 + 6,810 = 398,410); EMS p13 1,412,544 vs p5 1,432,149 (short 19,605: public safety 1,148,078 vs 1,169,363; debt service 123,836 vs 111,157 + 10,999 = 122,156). 82,575 - 522 + 19,605 = 101,658 = gap. General Fund (pp15-16, 2,626,576) and Other Governmental Funds (p14, 17,800 + 119,011 = 136,811) equal p5. No detail fix: the schedules print their own budgetary-basis actuals.
